posts.cooked:
We played a five-person game at Arsenal on Tuesday versus Apostate.

 

By round two we had seven relics out and the game was essentially lost.

 

BUT, we somehow managed to claw our way back for the win! Ra got out Imbued Fire and the power that enabled him to make all heroes immune to fire and then Nightmist let loose with a 4x4 Oblivion and the Argent Adept allowed Nighmist to play _another_ Oblivion while we were all immune (only 2x1 this time). With the +1 from imbued fire, that was 5x5x3x2 against every non-hero! Unity's Bots were taking the brunt of the damage from Apostate and Bunker had fired off a massive Omnicannon hit against Apostate earlier, so all of the sudden the game was within reach and we were able to pull it out.

posts.cooked: That was an awesome game, indeed.

We had just three people at Arsenal on Tuesday, but it was still lots of fun. As all of us were playtesters, we decided to use some of the in-progress decks, but decided to focus on just one deck per game and, perhaps surprisingly, decided to focus on the environment decks.

 

Three experienced players managed to lose to Voss using Haka, Nightmist, and Unity. I think we could have won that game. I should have played the Amulet of the Elder Gods before the Master of Magic. Mostly we were taken down by all of the Forced Deployments.

posts.name: Jhuntin1
posts.cooked:
The Forced Deployements were the problem. The first one we got cleared before killing any minions, but the other two both brought back 7 each including the annoying guard.

In hindsight, I'm convinced that I should have discarded my (Unity's) hand instead of Haka. I did no damage that game because I couldn't get out any of the generic bots despite what I thought was a good setup to make that happen.

posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked: Or if I'd put Nightmist's card (Astral Premonition) out that allowed her to stack Voss' deck, then we could have avoided the Forced Deployments.

posts.name: TheJayMann
posts.cooked: Or, if I had played Haka of Restoration that last turn, I'd have still been alive to potentially finish them off (if I'm drawing three cards for every destroyed environment card, I don't necessarily need the 25 cards in hand).

We had another great meetup today -- five people at Comic Carnival. Because of comings and goings we did two four-hero games.

In the first we gave Spite the smackdown. I, uh, really felt like winning so I suggested Spite and then chose to play The Wraith. I'd read about how well The Wraith did against him. She did not dissappoint. Stun Bolt! Smoke Bombs!

 

In the second we had some people trying out new, complex heroes for the first time (NightMist and Argent Adept), so I steered us towards playing GloomWeaver so it wouldn't be too hard of a game. With Absolute Zero in the mix (lots of slow build heroes!) I decided to go for Ra so we'd have some immediate damage ability. It was a bit touch and go in the beginnig, but we eventually cleared the board and coasted to victory.

 

Next date is, as always, the second Sunday of the month at 1pm -- Feb 10th. I, however, will not be able to attend, as I'll be out of town ... on an awesome nerd cruise! http://jococruisecrazy.com/
